text:
alex: heads-up — ran a quick internal loadtest against the hosted API to try and reproduce the customer 429/latency blips. sharing raw notes here so we can pick sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst windows.

maria: awesome, thanks. did you use the same token scopes as the customer (org-level vs project-level)? those change routing sometimes.

alex: yes used project key (same plan tier). test harness = k6 script + a small goroutine-based open-loop client for bursts. hitting /v1/completions endpoint, model=redwood-medium.

raj: can you paste the commands? want to replicate locally.

alex: sure — k6 scenario for steady state:
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 10m script.js
// script.js does basic text generation with 8 token prompt, no streaming
```
open-loop bursts I used a tiny go program that spawns N goroutines and sends M requests each as fast as possible, with random jitter.

ingrid: were you running from a single region? we should test cross-region too (latency can push queues).

alex: started in us-west-2. also tried eu-west-1 to check different capacity pools. results similar: most steady-state runs at ~180 RPM succeeded with p50 latency ~220ms, p95 ~480ms. when bursts hit (burst window = 10s, ~120 concurrent requests), we saw 429s and a cluster of 503s and some token queueing that pushed p95 to ~1.8s for ~15s.

katie: what headers did the API return on the 429s? any X-RateLimit-* headers or Retry-After?

alex: good question. here's a captured 429 response: 

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1610000000

{"error":"Rate limit exceeded - burst tokens exhausted"}
```

maria: that Reset epoch looks off — that's from our dev harness clock? make sure clocks were synced.

alex: yeah forgot to adjust, was running an old env but semantics still valid (burst token headers present). also saw some 503s with body: {"error":"server overloaded, fallback triggered"} when the queue depth hit the routing cap.

raj: did you test different burst bucket sizes? what values did you try for burst_window and burst_capacity?

alex: tested combinations:
- burst_window=10s, capacity=150 tokens -> 429 spikes when sustained >120 rps in window
- burst_window=30s, capacity=400 -> much smoother, but steady-state cost increased (more concurrency inside runtime)
- per-minute quotas (RPM) at 1000 vs 2000: at 1000 we hit per-minute throttles during prolonged traffic; at 2000 we rarely see 429s unless combined with high concurrency bursts

ingrid: interesting — so short window small capacity protects backend better but leads to more 429s. longer window trades safety for user experience. we should recommend conservative defaults but allow higher burst for Dedicated customers.

katie: any evidence that client-side retries improved overall success? I worry exponential backoff will hurt latency SLOs for interactive apps.

alex: naive retries (immediate or fixed 1s) just amplified load and generated more 503s. a jittered exponential backoff with initial 250ms and max 2s reduced total error rate by ~40% and smoothed downstream queues. but interactive chat latency p95 increased because of retries. for chat we should prefer streaming or smaller per-request token counts rather than retries.

maria: can you share the go reproducer snippet? would be useful for support to repro customer cases during escalation.

alex: pasted minimal reproducer below:
```go
// abridged: spawn G goroutines, each does M requests as fast as possible
for i:=0; i<G; i++ {
  go func(){
    for j:=0; j<M; j++ {
      req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
      req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer $KEY")
      req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
      client.Do(req)
    }
  }()
}
```

raj: nice. for the official benchmark suite we should capture: request timestamps, response codes, X-RateLimit-* headers, queue-length metrics from runtime, and per-model kernel saturation.

alex: agreed — added runtime debug tags for those runs. collected queue_depth and kv_cache_hit_rate. during worst-case the queue_depth spiked to ~650 and runtime started shedding.

ingrid: propose we set these defaults for hosted tenants (initial proposal):
- soft RPM: 1200 RPM per project
- hard RPM: 3000 RPM per project (burst allowed)
- steady-state RPS cap: 60 rps
- burst_window: 30s, burst_capacity: 350 tokens
- per-second guardrail: 150 rps absolute

maria: +1 but I'd lower soft RPM to 800 for free-tier orgs. also we need clear messaging in responses (Retry-After + human-friendly error).

katie: also add automatic canary where a tenant can request temporary burst boosts (90s) for migrations — recorded in audit logs.

alex: will spin up more runs to validate those numbers across models (small/med/large). current notes only for redwood-medium.

sre-bot: deploy-benchmark-job started: job_id=bench-1803456789-1, expected duration 45m.

raj: action items:
- alex: run cross-region for small/large models and post summarized numbers (p50/p95/p99, 429/503 counts) — due EOD tomorrow
- maria: draft default policy matrix per tier (free/dev/prod/dedicated) with soft/hard limits and burst policy text
- katie: add support-facing repro recipe to the runbook (include go + k6 + expected headers)
- ingrid: validate cost impact for 30s window across typical workloads (embeddings vs completions)

maria: one more thought: include a tiny client-side library snippet for best-effort backoff + hedged requests when latency > threshold. that will reduce perceived failed requests without overloading backend.

alex: agreed. I'll attach raw CSV output when bench finishes. posting follow-ups in this thread.

katie: thanks — great reproducible notes, this will help with the support escalations. :thumbsup:

ingrid: also flag for product — we should give enterprise admins ability to tweak burst params per project.

alex: noted. closing loop after bench complete.

sre-bot: job bench-1803456789-1 finished: summary uploaded to s3://bench-outputs/1803456789-summary.csv

alex: uploaded summary, linking here: https://internal.redwood/s3/bench-outputs/1803456789-summary.csv

raj: got it, will start running these in ci and add to perf-dashboard.

maria: thanks everyone.
